passages.note: Yes vote on a 15-week limit whose own construction clause creates no right and leaves the broader ban in force, so it shows only the restrictive side.
Co-sponsorship of the bill as filed; the bill's construction clause means it shows only the restrictive side.

passages.provision_quote: Except in a medical emergency, a physician may not intentionally or knowingly perform, induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion if the probable gestational age of the unborn human being has been determined to be greater than fifteen weeks.
passages.note: Operative 15-week limit with a medical-emergency exception, but Sec. 2 says it does not repeal section 13-3603 or make lawful any currently unlawful abortion, so no permitted stage is evidenced.
Yes vote on a bill that only repeals the old ban; it separates the sides but states no stage or exception rule.

passages.provision_quote: Section 13-3603, Arizona Revised Statutes, is repealed.
passages.note: A bare repeal of the older ban names no gestational limit or exception, so it does not match any rung's clauses.
His quoted belief in a 15-week law is in-term, but it gives no exception rule and does not say abortion should be allowed up to that point under the rung's terms.

rows.reasoning: Shope voted for and co-sponsored SB 1164 (a 15-week limit) and voted for HB 2677 (repeal of the older ban), and said he believes in a 15 week law, but SB 1164's construction clause creates no right and leaves the broader ban in force, and the repeal bill names no stage or exception. Together these show a side, not the rung that would "allow abortion during the first trimester, and after that only to protect the mother's health".

quotes.text: I voted yes, because I do believe in a 15 week [law], and that's what was in front of me
